items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I discovered Béla Bartók, and I did a lot of writing and composing music... I’m sure that it seeped in there just like my discovering Béla Bartók in music school (laughs) did

ctx.x: In five years in school Mozart got so much better, (laughs) I couldn’t… So that was then. And then I discovered Béla Bartók, and I did a lot of writing and composing music, and I kept playing this club on weekends.
Can I backtrack just a little bit?

items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Did your other musical colleagues do as much as you did to visit the cultures and try to communicate in the languages and…?

Yeah, I don’t, I don’t know if I actually did, but you tend to get immersed in it anyway. Like I had been to the… Remember Peter, the doorman? He was from Zagreb. And we played in his hometown. And it was fascinating. Again, what happens when… we did some pieces with a string quartet which I had written, and the verbal communication was kinda nil but their musical communication was great. And all over that area… I’ll get the atlas out in a minute. I forget. And, oh, I finally got to Budapest. Just a couple years…
